title: Bearings and Distances
seo_title: Bearings and Distances – JSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Read and use three-figure bearings; find back bearings; solve problems on bearings and distances, angles of elevation and depression, and scale drawings. (summary of the NERDC JSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 maths worksheets on bearings: three-figure bearings, back bearings, compass directions, angles of elevation and depression, and map scales. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bearings: clockwise from north, three figures
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A bearing is measured clockwise from north and written with three figures: 045°, 230°.
  • The back bearing is the bearing for the return journey: add or subtract 180°.
  • The angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal; the angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal.

Examples

Example

Bearing of B from A is 065°

65 + 180

Answer: Bearing of A from B is 245°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Measuring from eastAlways start from north.
Writing 65° instead of 065°Use three figures.
Mixing up elevation and depressionElevation looks up; depression looks down.

items.q: Aminat is facing west. She turns clockwise until she faces north-west. Through how many degrees does she turn?
items.e: From west (270°) to north-west (315°) clockwise: 45°.

items.q: Femi is facing south-west. He turns clockwise until he faces west. Through how many degrees does he turn?
items.e: From south-west (225°) to west (270°) clockwise: 45°.

items.q: Kunle is facing north-west. He turns clockwise until he faces south. Through how many degrees does he turn?
items.e: From north-west (315°) to south (180°) clockwise: 225°.

items.q: Kunle is facing south-east. He turns clockwise until he faces south. Through how many degrees does he turn?
items.e: From south-east (135°) to south (180°) clockwise: 45°.
